<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]], [[Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen]]
**At least 19 [[Republic of Yemen Armed Forces|Yemeni soldiers]] are killed by an [[Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula]] attack on a [[military camp]] in [[Abyan]], [[Yemen]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/08/al-qaeda-launches-deadly-attack-army-base-southern-yemen-190802081549242.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 Bangkok bombings]]
**Multiple bomb blasts hit [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], as [[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] attends a regional security summit. At least four people are injured. [https://www.dw.com/en/thailand-multiple-bomb-blasts-hit-bangkok/a-49859694 (DW)]

;Business and economy
*[[2019 Japan–South Korea trade dispute]]
**Japan announces the removal of South Korea from its list of most trusted trading partners, effective on August 28. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/japan-approves-removal-of-south-korea-from-preferred-trade-status-2019-08-01 (Marketwatch)]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] formally withdraws from the [[Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty]] with [[Russia]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/08/02/politics/nuclear-treaty-inf-us-withdraws-russia/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Zagreb shooting]]
**A gunman opens fire in the home of his ex-wife in [[Zagreb]], [[Croatia]], killing six, including a ten-year-old child. He later committed suicide after a manhunt. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-croatia-shooting-idUSKCN1US1FA (Reuters)] 
*[[Women's rights in Saudi Arabia]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] grants women the right to travel without permission from [[Women's rights in Saudi Arabia#Male guardians|a male guardian]], and expands their marriage and custodial rights in a series of royal decrees. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-women/saudi-arabia-lifts-travel-restrictions-on-women-grants-them-greater-control-idUSKCN1UR5TB?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Capital punishment in Japan]]
**Japan carries out the first executions this year, [[hanging]] Koichi Shoji, 64, who killed two women in 2001, and [[serial killer]] Yasunori Suzuki, 50, who killed three women between 2004 and 2005 in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2019/08/78df0b0b5344-breaking-news-japan-executes-2-death-row-inmates-fri-morning.html (Kyodo News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[UK House of Commons]]: [[2019 Brecon and Radnorshire by-election]]
**The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] gain the [[Brecon and Radnorshire (UK Parliament constituency)|Brecon and Radnorshire]] seat from the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]]. This marks the first time a seat has changed hands in a by-election triggered by a successful [[Recall of MPs Act 2015|recall petition]]. The working majority of the [[First Johnson ministry|Conservative government]] is reduced to one. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/aug/02/brecon-radnorshire-byelection-lib-dems-jane-dodds-win-cuts-johnson-commons-majority-to-one (''The Guardian'')]
*[[List of Donald Trump nominees who have withdrawn]]
**President Trump announces he will not nominate Representative [[John Ratcliffe (American politician)|John Ratcliffe]] to replace Dan Coats as [[Director of National Intelligence]] when he resigns on August 15, and plans to block Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence [[Susan M. Gordon|Sue Gordon]] from serving as acting director. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/02/us/politics/trump-ratcliffe-dni.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/02/us/politics/john-ratcliffe-sue-gordon.html (''The New York Times''²)]
*[[Murder of Alexandra Măceșanu]]
**[[Romania]]n [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Viorica Dăncilă]] sacks [[Ministry of National Education (Romania)|Minister of Education]] [[Ecaterina Andronescu]] for her controversial comments in a [[television]] interview about murdered 15-year-old girl [[Murder of Alexandra Măceșanu|Alexandra Măceșanu]], saying she was "taught not to get in cars with strangers". A 65-year-old man has since admitted killing Alexandra Măceșanu and another teenage girl who has been missing since April. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49210168 (BBC News)]
*[[Deforestation in Brazil]]
**[[Brazil]]'s [[National Institute for Space Research|National Space Research Institute]] Director-General [[Ricardo Galvão]] is dismissed from office as a result of the release of data showing a [[Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest|rise in Amazon deforestation]]. President [[Jair Bolsonaro]] has called the release of the data "irresponsible and sensationalist". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-49212115 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/aug/02/brazil-space-institute-director-sacked-in-amazon-deforestation-row (''The Guardian'')]

;Sports
*[[Argentina|Argentine]] footballer [[Lionel Messi]] is suspended from his [[Argentina national football team|national team]] for three months and fined US$50,000 for criticizing the [[CONMEBOL|South American Football Confederation]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/02/sports/soccer/lionel-messi-conmebol.html (''The New York Times'')]
